acceptance: A real DuckDB TPC-H Q1/Q6 CLI run with --capture-plans exports a bundle whose plans are retrievable through the MCP implementation using supported query-ID spellings, including when companion keys are Q1#0:power and Q6#0:power.
MCP retrieval preserves the correct plan identity for multiple stream/phase variants; missing or ambiguous requests have explicit outcomes and never silently select a different query.
A regression test consumes an actual exported bundle rather than a hand-built bare-key companion; existing CLI show-plan and comparison consumers continue to work.
context:
Reproduced on 2026-10-28: real DuckDB TPC-H SF 0.01, queries 1,6, iterations 1, seed 42, phases generate,load,power. show-plan and compare --include-plans succeeded; direct calls to _get_query_plan_impl returned no_plan for tree, summary and json. Exported companion keys were Q1#0:power and Q6#0:power. The ordinary loader rehydrated plans with verified fingerprint integrity.

Guardrails: do not change the .plans.json format, build_plans_payload, or loader keying; MCP adapts to them. Reuse the loader's plan indexing/lookup (benchbox/core/results/loader.py _index_plan_entries/_lookup_plan_entry or load_result_file) instead of a third lookup convention. A bare ID that maps to several stream/phase variants must not silently pick one: return the variant list or require a qualifier. Keep MCP read-only annotations and error envelope shape.

Verification rubric: (1) focused regression test fails before the change and passes after; (2) uv run -- python -m pytest -n 0 on the touched plan test modules passes; (3) make comment-policy-check and ruff/typecheck on touched files pass; (4) a runtime smoke on the real surface described in acceptance is recorded in the PR body.
description: MCP get_query_plan reports no_plan for plans that the CLI can display from the same real result bundle. analytics._get_query_plan_impl directly indexes queries by a normalized bare query ID, while build_plans_payload emits query/stream/phase-qualified keys and can retain prefixed IDs. Reuse the canonical result loader and its identity rules rather than introducing another companion lookup convention. Preserve a defined selection policy when several stream or phase variants exist.
